title: Principal crossed homomorphisms from a smooth diagonalizable group into an additive subgroup
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. All group schemes are affine $F$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $D$ be smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and diagonalizable: for a finitely generated abelian group $M$ there is an isomorphism $D\simeq\operatorname{Spec}F[M]$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], where $F[M]$ has basis $e_m$, multiplication $e_me_n=e_{m+n}$, comultiplication $e_m\mapsto e_m\otimes e_m$, counit $e_m\mapsto1$, and antipode $e_m\mapsto e_{-m}$. Let $\chi:D\to\mathbf G_m$ be a group-scheme homomorphism, and let $N\subseteq\mathbf G_a$ be a closed subgroup scheme [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup, def-weil-closed-immersion] stable under multiplication by $\chi$: for every commutative $F$-algebra $A$, $d\in D(A)$ and $x\in N(A)\subseteq A$, one has $\chi_A(d)x\in N(A)$. Here $\mathbf G_a(A)=(A,+)$ and $\mathbf G_m(A)=A^\times$ [def-sc-gm-ga]. If an $F$-scheme morphism $f:D\to N$ satisfies
$$f_A(dd')=f_A(d)+\chi_A(d)f_A(d')$$
for every commutative $F$-algebra $A$ and $d,d'\in D(A)$, then there exists $a\in N(F)$ such that
$$f_A(d)=a_A-\chi_A(d)a_A$$
for every such $A,d$, where $a_A$ is the scalar extension of $a$. No smoothness or connectedness of $N$, and no connectedness of $D$, is assumed.

source.place: Proposition 15.3, printed p.303 (commutative unipotent group varieties); nonsmooth additive subgroup form obtained by factoring the morphism from smooth D through N_red, as in the smooth-quotient scope of Summary 16.29, printed p.334.

proof.text: Use the torsion-kernel lemma with $p=1$ in characteristic zero and $p=\operatorname{char}F$ otherwise: $H_n=D[n](F)$ is finite of order $c_n$ coprime to $p$, and vanishing on all $H_n$ detects regular functions on $D$. Multiplication by $c_n$ is bijective on $N(F)\subset F$. Indeed, for $s\in N(F)$ put $b=s/c_n\in F$, since $c_n$ is nonzero in $F$. If $N=\mathbf G_a$ then $b\in N(F)$. Otherwise the additive-subgroup polynomial lemma supplies a monic additive $P$ with $N(F)=\{x:P(x)=0\}$. Repeated additivity gives $c_nP(b)=P(c_nb)=P(s)=0$, so $P(b)=0$ and $b\in N(F)$. Injectivity follows by cancellation in $F$. No smoothness of $N$ is used.

source.place: Proposition 15.3, printed p.303, finite-subgroup averaging; Proposition 12.3 and Remark 12.5, pp.231–232; Theorem 12.32, p.242. Division in an arbitrary closed additive subgroup and the divisibility-directed compatibility are written out here.

proof.text: Fix an admissible $n$ and put $s_n=\sum_{y\in H_n}f_F(y)\in N(F)$. For $x\in H_n$, summing the crossed identity and permuting $y\mapsto xy$ gives $s_n=c_nf_F(x)+\chi_F(x)s_n$. Choose $a_n\in N(F)$ with $c_na_n=s_n$, as justified above. The scalar $c_n$ is nonzero in $F$, so cancellation in $F$ gives $f_F(x)=(1-\chi_F(x))a_n$ for every $x\in H_n$. This is exactly the finite-subgroup averaging of Milne 15.3, with the sign $f(x)=a_n-\chi(x)a_n$.

source.place: Proposition 15.3, printed p.303, finite-subgroup averaging; Proposition 12.3 and Remark 12.5, pp.231–232; Theorem 12.32, p.242. Division in an arbitrary closed additive subgroup and the divisibility-directed compatibility are written out here.

proof.text: If $\chi$ is the trivial character, the averaging identity says $f_F(x)=0$ on every $H_n$. Apply the torsion-kernel lemma's regular-function test to the pullback of the additive coordinate under $D\xrightarrow fN\hookrightarrow\mathbf G_a$: it is zero in $F[M]$. Morphisms to $\mathbf G_a$ are determined by this coordinate, so $f_A(d)=0$ for all $A,d$, and $a=0\in N(F)$ works.

source.place: Proposition 15.3, printed p.303, finite-subgroup averaging; Proposition 12.3 and Remark 12.5, pp.231–232; Theorem 12.32, p.242. Division in an arbitrary closed additive subgroup and the divisibility-directed compatibility are written out here.

proof.text: Otherwise $\chi^*(t)-1$ is a nonzero regular function on $D$. The same torsion-kernel test supplies an admissible $n_0$ and $h\in H_{n_0}$ with $\chi_F(h)\ne1$. Fix $a=a_{n_0}$. For any admissible $n$, set $m=\operatorname{lcm}(n,n_0)$, which is admissible and satisfies $H_n,H_{n_0}\subseteq H_m$. Evaluating the averaging formula for $m$ and $n_0$ at $h$ gives $(1-\chi_F(h))(a_m-a)=0$, hence $a_m=a$. Thus $f_F(x)=(1-\chi_F(x))a$ on every $H_n$. Apply the torsion-kernel test to the regular function $f^*(y)-a(1-\chi^*(t))$ to obtain equality in $F[M]$, hence the stated equality after every $F$-algebra extension. The right side belongs to $N(A)$ by scalar stability and subtraction in its subgroup, and $N(A)\hookrightarrow A$ is injective, so this is the required identity in $N$, not just in $\mathbf G_a$.

lean.statement: theorem smooth_diagonal_additive_crossed_principal {F : Type u} [Field F] [IsAlgClosed F] (D N : Over (Spec (.of F))) [GrpObj D] [GrpObj N] [IsAffine D.left] [LocallyOfFiniteType D.hom] [QuasiCompact D.hom] [IsAffine N.left] [LocallyOfFiniteType N.hom] [QuasiCompact N.hom] [Smooth D.hom] (hdiag : ∃ (M : Type u) (_ : AddCommGroup M) (_ : AddGroup.FG M), Nonempty (Grp.mk D ≅ diagonalizableGroup F M)) (chi : D ⟶ multiplicative F) [IsMonHom chi] (i : N ⟶ additive F) [IsClosedSubgroupScheme i] (hstable : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra F A] (d : affine F A ⟶ D) (x : A), (∃ z : affine F A ⟶ N, z ≫ i = additiveCoordinatePoint F A x) → ∃ z : affine F A ⟶ N, z ≫ i = additiveCoordinatePoint F A (multiplicativeCoordinateValue F (d ≫ chi) * x)) (f : D ⟶ N) (hcrossed : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra F A] (d d' : affine F A ⟶ D) (x y : A), d ≫ f ≫ i = additiveCoordinatePoint F A x → d' ≫ f ≫ i = additiveCoordinatePoint F A y → (d * d') ≫ f ≫ i = additiveCoordinatePoint F A (x + multiplicativeCoordinateValue F (d ≫ chi) * y)) : ∃ a : F, (∃ z : affine F F ⟶ N, z ≫ i = additiveCoordinatePoint F F a) ∧ ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra F A] (d : affine F A ⟶ D), d ≫ f ≫ i = additiveCoordinatePoint F A (algebraMap F A a - multiplicativeCoordinateValue F (d ≫ chi) * algebraMap F A a)
